subject.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus

question: How should existing no-provenance heartbeat transcripts and their derived corpus entries be repaired on upgrade?
rationale: The prospective provenance marker cannot identify data written by shipped releases, while text-only cross-message inference could suppress legitimate user conversations; repository history does not establish which migration or rebuild policy maintainers intend.

options.title: Add a safe rebuild path
options.body: Use trusted session metadata or another bounded owner-defined signal to invalidate and rebuild affected corpus state without rewriting arbitrary user text.

options.title: Accept future-only behavior
options.body: Narrow the PR’s claim to newly recorded heartbeat turns and explicitly accept that historical pollution ages out without automatic repair.

options.title: Redesign turn classification
options.body: Introduce a canonical runtime-owned turn classification that supports both future transcript writes and a reliable legacy migration.

recommendation.title: Add a safe rebuild path
recommendation.body: Use trusted session metadata or another bounded owner-defined signal to invalidate and rebuild affected corpus state without rewriting arbitrary user text.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent transcript-corpus and Dreaming metadata architecture places this persisted-state decision most naturally at this ownership boundary.
